rv.q: Top Girls has never seemed more hilarious, or wrenching.
But it's lit up by fine, bruising performances, not least Katherine Kingsley's bright, brittle Marlene.
In each section there is something extraordinary. Yet the movement of Turner's production is sometimes flaccid, and I am no longer convinced that this is Churchill's best play.
Lyndsey Turner's overstretched, underpowered revival... focus and laughs are lost.
If Act I has not bored the audience into a rigid coma, the next scene completes the job.
Dazzlingly perceptive... Enjoyable high-definition revival of Caryl Churchill's 1982 feminist classic.
The cast of this revival, directed by Lyndsey Turner, is on sparkling form here, and the laughs come thick and fast...'
An excellent production of a 1982 play still relevant in a world where painfully little has changed.
Lyndsey Turner directs an enjoyable version of this over-rated work.
Top Girls remains an important, forever relevant and still surprising play, even in a production that doesn't always hit its marks.
In such a production, even with a few points muffled, it doesn't get much better than this.
Yet none of this detracts much from the pleasure of watching compelling ideas get such a theatrically canny staging.
While the play itself and its political connotations hold relevance today, this production leaves quite a bit to be desired.

cn.t: Churchill's 1982 masterpiece receives mixed reviews in Turner's National Theatre revival. Critics praise the play's enduring relevance and audacious opening scene, but some find the production flat or dated for 2019.
